user: When are night court services available and what types of matters are heard in there?
assistant: Night Court services at the Carol Miller Justice Center are available on the 2nd Wednesday of each month from 4:00 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. If the second Wednesday of the month is a court holiday, Night Court will be held on the 2nd Thursday of that same month. During Night Court, Traffic arraignments and Small Claims trials are heard in person and via video. Mediation and Advisory Services for Small Claims and Unlawful Detainer matters are available in person and via video utilizing Zoom. However, please note that interpreter services are not currently available during the Night Court hours.
user: The Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse
assistant: The Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse houses the main administrative offices of the court, as well as containing trial courtrooms, the department of the Presiding Judge, and the general civil and criminal case processing support units.
The Hall of Justice Building in the immediate vicinity of the Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse also provides court services. Located on the second floor at 813 6th Street are Departments 53 and 54, hearing general civil law and motion matters. Located at 813 6th Street, first floor, is Department 59 where general civil settlement conferences are heard.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Is there a Small Claims Court?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
Yes, there is a Small Claims Court. Small Claims cases are heard at the Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse and during Night Court sessions at the Carol Miller Justice Center. Night Court services are available on the second Wednesday of each month from 4:00 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. Small Claims trials are conducted in person and via video during these Night Court sessions. 
The Small Claims Court provides a special venue for resolving disputes quickly and inexpensively. The rules are simple, and the hearings are informal. Attorneys are not permitted to represent parties during the proceedings, but you may consult a lawyer for advice before attending Small Claims Court. In this court, disputes are settled in a fair, swift, and cost-effective manner.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]

There is no limit for claims involving COVID-19 rental debt. [S7] However, the provided evidence does not establish whether Small Claims Court is located at the Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse.

If you want to sue a tenant for COVID-19 rental debt, get step-by-step instructions on how to start a case.

If you were sued for COVID-19 rental debt (you were served a Plaintiff's Claim and Order to Go to Small Claims Court (COVID-19 Rental Debt) (form SC-500), find out your options.

Small claims is a cheaper and faster process

The costs. The filing fee for a small claims case is between $30-$100. If you can’t afford the fee, you can ask the court for a fee waiver.

Q:  May I sue for the recovery of property?
A:  Small claims court is for the recovery of money only.

Q:  How do I file a claim?
A:  The forms to file a small claims case can be located on the court website under Online Forms by selecting the Judicial Council hyperlink.

 If you do not have access to a computer, you may either come directly to the clerkâs office to fill out the appropriate paperwork or have the paperwork 
 mailed to you by sending in your request along with a self-addressed stamped envelope. There is also a Small Claims Kiosk in the clerkâs office where 
 you can complete the claim form online by answering questions.

Limited civil cases are cases for $35,000 or less

For lawsuits for $12,500 or less, the person suing (plaintiff) may be able to file in small claims court instead. Business entities, like a corporation, can sue for up to $6,250 in small claims court. If you're suing about COVID-19 rental debt, there is no limit to how much you can sue for in small claims court. These cases are typically faster, less complicated, and less expensive than a limited civil case.
